_notes: v0.4 retune: split broad regulatory/security keywords into 'core' (force opus, narrow) and 'domain' (min sonnet, broad). Prevents every TDS/GST/auth phase from auto-escalating to critical+opus. v0.14.35: haiku tier removed (configured but unreachable in practice); tier_caps deleted with it. v0.14.36: prefer_top_for_critical set false — complexity scoring was a weak escalation proxy; failure-driven escalation (phase fails → re-run on opus) replaces it. Flip back to true to restore, then check /spend. v0.15: haiku tier reinstated for mechanical overhead tasks now that config/defaults.json's model_routing.tier_models carries a haiku entry, making it reachable end-to-end. Keyword-rule matches now resolve by explicit precedence instead of array order: force_tier always wins outright; else the most restrictive matched max_tier cap wins over the highest matched min_tier floor (floor applies first, then the cap is re-applied over it); complexity escalation (prefer_top_for_critical) remains the lowest-priority step, unchanged. v0.17 (schema 3): 4th tier 'fable' (claude-fable-5) — regulatory-core/security-core force_tier retuned opus → fable (wrong = legal/silent-expensive consequences; one top-tier sample earns its cost there). Fable can return a refusal stop_reason on security-adjacent content; the escalation ladder treats that like any other is_error (opus marker re-run), so a refused fable call degrades, not deadlocks. hard_floors entries may now be conditional {tier, when:{min_*}} objects (size-gated opus floors): the floor applies when ANY listed size signal meets its threshold, applies unconditionally when the caller supplied no signals (fail-safe), and is skipped otherwise — small briefs plan on the sonnet baseline and rely on the plan-validate + coverage-BLOCKER regen backstop; a 0-2-candidate audit scan needs no opus adjudicator.

_hard_floors_comment: v0.17 size-gated opus floors. plan-creation/roadmap: opus only for large briefs (≥12k chars OR ≥8 numbered FRs — signals computed from the active brief in runGuide); small briefs draft on sonnet with the plan-validate coverage gate as backstop. audit: opus adjudication only when the two-stage scan produced ≥3 candidates (count re-routed after the scan stage in runTwoStageAudit); the single-call 'audit' path (audit.two_stage:false with no diff to scope to) passes no signals, so the floor still applies there (fail-safe). Plain string floors remain unconditional. phase-32 (MI-10): 'audit-incremental' (diff-scoped re-audits) deliberately has NO entry here — that absence IS the feature. Before phase-32, incremental re-audits routed under the SAME 'audit' key, so the fail-safe-when-no-signals rule above applied unconditionally to every incremental re-audit (they never supply candidate counts), paying opus over an already O(diff) input on every bug-round re-audit up to max_chain_rounds. Splitting incremental re-audits onto their own task id with no hard_floors entry lets them route on the sonnet baseline; the unchanged-HEAD forced-full, force_full_every_n periodic full, and the two-stage full audit's own opus floor (candidates>=3) remain the safety valves against sonnet under-judging a fix-verification. Do not add an 'audit-incremental' entry here without re-checking /spend first.

user_preferences._escalation_scope_note: v0.14.37: keyword + complexity escalation applies only to escalation_tasks (top-level key). Guide/overhead tasks route on baselines + floors.
